instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Retry unit U17 (briefs/U17.md); the file is unchanged since before the run. Test-only change: change no source file. Keep cases (1)-(3) exactly as round 5 wrote them (they passed). Round 4 failed because elements created with API.setElements are never captured by history, so undo removed the whole element. Add `describe("per-range text styling", ...)` at the end of the file. Anchoring: exactly two edits, each with a unique search text. (a) Add `import { actionChangeStrokeColor } from "../actions/actionProperties";` right after the unique line `import { actionTextAutoResize } from "../actions/actionTextAutoResize";`. Do NOT import actionChangeHighlightColor (it no longer exists). Also import KEYS / act only if not already imported (check the existing import blocks from "@excalidraw/common" and "../tests/test-utils"; add to them rather than duplicating). (b) Search for the unique line `      expect(h.elements.filter((el) => !el.isDeleted)).toHaveLength(0);` (inside it("removes a plain text in a single undo")) and replace it with itself + `\n    });\n  });\n\n  describe("per-range text styling", () => {` + the new cases, so the file's remaining `    });\n  });\n});` closes the last new it(), the new describe and the outer describe. In EVERY case create the text with the text tool: `UI.clickTool("text"); mouse.clickAt(100, 100) (or new Pointer("mouse").clickAt(100, 100)); let editor = await getTextEditor(); updateTextEditor(editor, "Hello world"); Keyboard.exitTextEditor(editor);` then reopen: `API.setSelectedElements([h.elements[0]]); Keyboard.keyPress(KEYS.ENTER); editor = await getTextEditor();`. Select with `act(() => editor.setSelectionRange(0, 5));`. Colour: `act(() => h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionChangeStrokeColor, "ui", { currentItemStrokeColor: "#e03131" }))`; highlight: `act(() => h.app.actionManager.executeAction(actionChangeStrokeColor, "ui", { highlightColor: "#ffec99" }))`. Cases (keep all of them): (1) live display: with selection 0..5 apply colour and highlight, then with h.state.editingTextElement still set assert editor.style.color === "transparent", JSON.parse(editor.dataset.textRanges!) holds the range, and h.app.renderer.getRenderableElements(...).elementsMap.get(id)?.textRanges holds it (as in round 4's passing version); (2) live typing shifts and deletes ranges; (3) a collapsed selection (setSelectionRange(3,3)) recolours the whole element's strokeColor and leaves no own 'textRanges' property; (4) undo/redo (user revise at Gate 3, round 6; this is the ONLY case whose expectations change from round 5, where cases 1-3 passed in all 3 attempts and case 4 failed with `expected 3 to be 2` at the stack-size check): after reopening, record `const before = (h.history as any).undoStack.length;`, select 0..5, apply the highlight, exit with Keyboard.exitTextEditor(editor); assert h.elements[0].textRanges is set and `(h.history as any).undoStack.length === before + 2`. Put a comment above that assertion: the styling is one entry (textRanges plus the selection leaving the element), and exiting the editor adds the existing selection-only entry (selectedElementIds {} -> {id: true}), as recolouring the whole element while editing also does. Measured on this tree: stack 1 -> 2 on the highlight -> 3 on exit. Then the FIRST Keyboard.undo(): add the comment `// the first undo only restores the selection`; assert the element still exists, is not deleted, and its textRanges is still set. Then the SECOND Keyboard.undo(): the element still exists and is not deleted, its textRanges is undefined and `"textRanges" in el` is false. Then ONE Keyboard.redo(): textRanges is restored (start 0, end 5, highlight #ffec99). Read elements via h.elements after each step (they are replaced, not mutated). Do not change existing tests; no toMatchSnapshot.

The file's current text is under Inputs, marked "current text"; your edits apply to exactly that text.

## Answer
Return ONLY a JSON object {"path": "packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx", "edits": [{"search": "<text copied exactly from the current text>", "replace": "<its replacement>"}]} with no other text. Each search must appear exactly once in the current text; the edits apply in order.
If the file does not exist yet, or the change rewrites most of it, return {"path": "packages/excalidraw/wysiwyg/textWysiwyg.test.tsx", "content": "<the complete file>"} instead.
